problems.statement: Pay alone (a general under-market wage) explains the jump in teller turnover from 28% to 47%.

Teller pay is below competing offers and is a real, chronic contributor, especially to hiring (offer declines, slower time-to-fill) and to some exits; its size is unmeasured because no market study exists since 2023.

Scheduling and work-demand changes introduced from March 2026 (second mandatory Saturday and longer Saturday hours at all 46 branches, plus the announced and later live ShiftWise scheduling) are the main driver of the added turnover, with the monthly step occurring in March and schedule complaints rising from 19% to 48%.
The ShiftWise scheduling system itself, rather than the firm-wide Saturday change, is the main cause of the increase.
A tighter local labor market and industry-wide turnover pressure explain part of the rise, roughly 5 of the 19 points, and probably part of the pre-March elevation.
Turnover is driven by a handful of poor branch managers, so PIPs and bonus withholding are warranted.
The turnover increase is a measurement artifact from the HRIS migration or inconsistent counting.

Vacancies are being covered with overtime, which is a consequence of turnover and may reinforce it by overloading remaining tellers; new-hire churn (under-12-month leavers up from 41% to 58%) is feeding the loop.
Turnover was already about 50% above prior-year pace before the March changes (11.0 vs 7.2 per month), and the cause of that baseline rise is not identified.

causalClaims.to: the FY2026 increase in teller turnover (28% to 47%)

causalClaims.from: Second Saturday and extended Saturday hours (March 2026)

causalClaims.to: higher quit rates and competing-offer exits

actions.action: Approve a blanket 15% across-the-board teller increase ($2.6M recurring, not practically reversible) on the current evidence.
actions.rationale: Pay does not explain the change in turnover, the market position is unmeasured, and a permanent cost would be locked in while the likely scheduling cause stays unaddressed.

actions.action: Request the branch-level separation report with corrected manager dates now (due about 2026-12-01), split by ShiftWise vs non-ShiftWise and by month.
actions.rationale: It is cheap, arrives before the December 10 budget lock, and directly tests the Saturday vs ShiftWise vs manager explanations.

actions.action: Buy the State Bankers Association 2026 teller pay module or commission a quick market study, and compare Teller I rates with competitors.
actions.rationale: It replaces anecdotal postings with data, so any pay adjustment can be sized and targeted.

actions.action: Hold the 2027-01-11 ShiftWise expansion to the remaining 27 branches pending the branch analysis, using the 30-day no-fee date-change clause (notice by about 2026-12-12).
actions.rationale: It is reversible and free, and avoids repeating a possibly harmful schedule change at the other 52% of tellers.

actions.action: Put a reserve or contingency line for targeted teller pay and schedule fixes in the FY2027 budget before December 10, to be released through the January 18 structure review (approval by January 5).
actions.rationale: It keeps the pay option open without committing $2.6M to an unproven diagnosis.

actions.action: Review the second-Saturday rotation and the 7-day posting window and give tellers more predictable schedules, for example 2 to 3 week postings or voluntary Saturday swaps, testing at a few branches.
actions.rationale: Schedule is the best-supported controllable change, but the Saturday and ShiftWise effects are not yet separated.

actions.action: Place the five named branch managers on PIPs and withhold bonuses where turnover exceeds 45% using the PeopleCore manager field.
actions.rationale: The manager field is stale for seven branches (three of the five named), so it would penalize the wrong people, and managers at ShiftWise branches cannot control schedules.

actions.action: Make a targeted pay adjustment (for example Teller I starting rate) if the market study confirms a gap, effective January 2027.
actions.rationale: Reasonable only once the market position is known, and offer-decline and posting data suggest a real but unsized gap.

actions.action: Track vacancy-related overtime and new-hire retention (under 12 months) as indicators of the vacancy spiral.
actions.rationale: VAC-COVER hours of 9,760 are a cost and a possible burnout driver; these metrics show whether fixes work.

nextEvidence: Branch-level separations by month with corrected manager dates, split ShiftWise vs non-ShiftWise and by Saturday impact, compared with pre-March baselines (ready about 2026-12-01).
External teller pay benchmark (State Bankers Association 2026 module or new market study) against current Teller I starting rate and midpoint.
Complete exit and stay interviews or a full-staff pulse survey with a response rate well above 19%, asking about schedule notice, Saturdays and pay, plus destination of leavers.
output.summary: The pay-only diagnosis does not fit. Pay ranked first in exit surveys in both years (58% and 61%), so it cannot explain a rise. Monthly separations stepped up in March, when the second Saturday and longer hours hit all branches and ShiftWise was announced. Schedule complaints rose from 19% to 48%. Peers rose only 5 points, so the market explains part. The manager theory rests on a stale data field. Do not approve a blanket $2.6M raise or manager PIPs. Order the branch report, get market pay data, hold the ShiftWise expansion, and keep a targeted-pay reserve.
